source_user: Calculation case 499: a model has 48 layers, 6 KV heads, head dimension 64, sequence length 1536, and INT8 KV values. Estimate bytes for one request's K/V cache. Show the formula and report GiB.
source_assistant: Use 2 × layers × sequence_length × KV_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_value. Here this is 2 × 48 × 1536 × 6 × 64 × 1 = 56623104 bytes = 0.052734 GiB. This excludes allocator metadata and other runtime memory.
corrected_answer: Assuming one request retains dense, separate K and V for every layer and token, with nominal INT8 storage of 1 byte/value and no prefix sharing, paging, eviction, or width-changing packing, the logical payload is 2 (K,V) × 48 layers × 1536 tokens × 6 KV heads × 64 values/head × 1 byte/value = 56,623,104 bytes = 0.052734 GiB (2^30 bytes/GiB). This is a logical estimate, not allocator-visible runtime memory: INT8 scales/metadata, padding, pages, fragmentation, batching, concurrency, cache policy, and implementation layout can change actual use. Confirm the deployed representation and dimensions; measure allocated/reserved memory, capacity/OOM or eviction, correctness, prefill/decode latency, throughput, and tail latency at the target lengths and concurrency.
risks: INT8 scales or other quantization metadata may add storage beyond the nominal one-byte payload.
Logical payload and runtime allocation can differ materially; the deployment may not match the stated dimensions or cache policy.
evidence_required: Verify layers, KV heads, head dimension, sequence length, dtype/representation, layout, cache policy, batching, concurrency, and runtime version.
Run matched memory, capacity/OOM or eviction, correctness, prefill/decode latency, throughput, and tail-latency measurements.

source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 1: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer: Assumptions: define a fixed model build, serving engine, hardware, tokenizer, prompt/generation distributions, concurrency levels, and success thresholds; report results separately for prefill and decode. Falsifiable hypothesis: under the stated workload and warm, steady-state conditions, the proposed serving configuration changes TTFT/TPOT and capacity without violating correctness or the agreed P99 latency target. Use a randomized, paired A/B experiment with the same replayed requests, randomized order, isolated hosts, fixed batching/scheduling and sampling settings, warm-up exclusion, and enough repetitions for confidence intervals. Measure request-level timestamps for queue entry, dispatch, prefill start/end, first token, each decode token, completion, cancellations, and errors; report TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end latency, throughput (requests and tokens), queueing delay, utilization, batch sizes, and P50/P95/P99/P99.9 tails, stratified by prompt/output length and concurrency. Capture GPU/CPU memory, utilization, power/thermal state, cache behavior, OOMs, evictions, retries, and traces. Control or record model/runtime versions, kernels, precision, hardware, background load, network, and workload mix. Analyze paired deltas with uncertainty and stop/rollback if correctness, error rate, OOM/eviction rate, or P99 exceeds predefined limits; do not claim causality if confounders or sample size prevent it.
risks: Workload mix, warm-up, queueing, batching, hardware state, or background load can confound comparisons.
Aggregate averages can hide tail regressions; TTFT and TPOT must not be conflated.
A performance change may trade off correctness, capacity, cost, or reliability.
evidence_required: Record the exact model, engine, hardware, versions, precision, scheduler, limits, workload distribution, concurrency, and experiment randomization.

Collect repeated paired trials with request-level traces, warm-up policy, confidence intervals, stratified latency/throughput/tail metrics, resource telemetry, errors, OOMs/evictions, and correctness checks.
Predeclare thresholds and rollback criteria, then rerun any anomalous or materially changed result under the same controlled conditions.
